description: Fetch a filtered slice of a Eurostat dataset as decoded observations: dimension codes and labels, numeric value, OBS_FLAG status and CONF_STATUS confidentiality marker. Returns a deterministic inline prefix (preview_limit) beside totals over the whole match; filters and period inputs shrink the match itself. Read dimension codes with eurostat_get_dataset_info and their values with eurostat_get_dimension_values first. Filter large slices: Eurostat refuses an oversized query (extraction_too_big) or prepares a large one in the background (async_response). On a deployment with a dataframe canvas, a match above 5,000 observations, or any match with stage=true, is staged as a SQL table (tableName). For a whole dataset, eurostat_download_dataset is the cheaper route.

canvas_id.description: A canvasId from an earlier staging response, to stage this result beside its tables for joins; omit for a fresh canvas. Used only when this call stages.

dataset_code.description: Dataset code (e.g., "nama_10_gdp"). DS-* codes (Comext trade and PRODCOM, in any case) work too; their trade flows mix annual and monthly series, so filter freq.

filters.description: Map of dimension code → values to keep, e.g. {"unit": ["CP_MEUR"], "geo": ["DE", "FR"]}; eurostat_get_dimension_values lists the values. Keys match in any case and must be dimensions: one naming a request control (lang, format, geoLevel, sinceTimePeriod, untilTimePeriod, lastTimePeriod) is rejected as invalid_dimension. An empty array or a blank value is no filter. A value holding "+" is split into separate values (OR); one holding "." matches nothing, since no Eurostat code contains it. Leave out "geo" when geo_level is set, and "time"/"time_period" when a period input is. A value that matches nothing is named in unmatchedValues, and a valid one with no cell in the selected periods in emptyValues; neither is an error.

geo_level.description: NUTS level to keep, mutually exclusive with filters.geo: "aggregate" (EU/EA totals), "country" (member and candidate states), "nuts1", "nuts2" or "nuts3". A code of the level with no cell in the match is named in emptyValues.

last_n_periods.description: Select the N most recent time positions of the dataset. N counts back from the dataset's latest period, not this slice's, so a slice that lags can come back short or empty; a notice names each selected period with no cell. Mutually exclusive with since_period and until_period.

preview_limit.description: Observations returned inline, from the start of the dataset's cell order. Default 25; positive integers above 500 are clamped to 500 with a notice. Shortens only the inline prefix: the counts, timeRange and staged rows still cover the whole match.

since_period.description: Start of the range, inclusive: YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-Qn (1–4), YYYY-Sn (1–2), YYYY-Tn (1–3), YYYY-Mnn (01–12), YYYY-Wnn (up to 53) or YYYY-Dnnn (up to 366), e.g. "2020", "2023-Q1", "2024-01". Any form works on any dataset, but Eurostat keeps only periods wholly inside the range, per frequency: a bound that falls inside a period excludes it, and a notice names that period when the response shows its frequency. A one-day range (both bounds on the same day) selects that day alone. A malformed or non-existent period, or a since_period after until_period, fails as invalid_period.

stage.description: Stage the whole match as a SQL table whatever its size; by default only a match above 5,000 observations is staged. Without a dataframe canvas, a notice says nothing was staged.

until_period.description: End of the range, inclusive (e.g., "2024"), in the forms and under the wholly-inside rule of since_period. Omit for data through the latest period.

name: eurostat_query_dataset

absentCellCount.description: Periods the matched series lack: for each series (one combination of the non-time dimensions) with a cell in the match, the periods of a frequency it carries where Eurostat publishes no cell for it. Only periods from that frequency's first to its latest period with a cell in any series count; one before or after that span is named in the notice instead. A series lacks no period of a frequency it does not carry (an annual series lacks no months). Absent cells are not observations: obsCount, missingObsCount, observations and staged rows leave them out.

filters.description: Filters sent to Eurostat: "+" values split, blank values and empty dimensions dropped.

canvasId.description: Canvas holding the staged table; pass it as canvas_id to the dataframe tools or a later staging call. Omitted when nothing was staged.

dimensionsUsed.description: Dimension codes in the response, in order.

emptyValues.description: Selected values the dataset has but this match carries no cell for, by dimension: filter values as sent, and under geo_level each "geo" code of that level with no cell. Never a time value or one in unmatchedValues. Such a value can have data in other periods or beside other filter values. Omitted when every selected value has a cell.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `not_found`: The dataset code does not exist. `no_results`: No cell of a valid dataset carries a value or flag for the filters and period range. The error names what it can: the filter values that matched nothing (data.unmatchedValues) with, when the dataset's values can be read, the codes of each such dimension holding at most 25 or a value search (data.validValues); the selected periods with no value (data.matchedPeriods, the newest 24; data.matchedPeriodCount counts all); whether a range misses the coverage, holds no whole period or no published one; and geo_level when it likely selects no code. `invalid_period`: A period bound is not an accepted form or names a period that does not exist, or since_period starts after until_period ends (bounds of different frequencies compare by day). Checked before any request. `async_response`: Eurostat is preparing this extraction in the background and serves the identical query minutes later. The server sends the request once and does not repeat it. `extraction_too_big`: Eurostat refused the query as too large to serve (its extraction limit is 5,000,000 rows); the same query is refused again. `invalid_dimension`: A filter key is not a dimension of this dataset; the error names every such key and lists the dataset's dimensions in key order, or only the key Eurostat names when the structure cannot be read. A request-control key (see filters) fails here before any request, naming the input that sets it. `conflicting_params`: Mutually exclusive inputs were combined: filters.geo with geo_level, since_period/until_period with last_n_periods, or a "time"/"time_period" filter with a period input. `canvas_not_found`: canvas_id is unknown or has expired. `upstream_fault`: The Statistics API failed or could not be reached on every attempt; retryable says whether a later call can succeed. `retry_deadline_exceeded`: The Statistics API did not finish within the server's request deadline (30 s by default), every attempt included: an uncached extraction or a large answer can take longer. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

missingObsCount.description: Matched observations with no numeric value, over the whole match: cells published without a number, carrying a flag, a confidentiality marker or text. A wholly confidential slice makes this equal obsCount without the data being absent. A period with no cell at all counts in absentCellCount instead.

notice.description: Disclosures, when any apply: a period a bound excludes, unmatchedValues, emptyValues (up to 24 named), last_n_periods positions with no cell (the newest 24 named), periods before or after a frequency's span and absent cells (see absentCellCount), the inline preview, and staging, with the eurostat_dataframe_describe then eurostat_dataframe_query sequence.

obsCount.description: Observations matched, over the whole match.

observations.description: The first preview_limit observations in the dataset's cell order: the leading dimension combinations, not a sample and not necessarily the latest periods. tableName, when set, holds every matched row.

confStatus.description: CONF_STATUS marker, a separate codelist from status: present when Eurostat restricts the cell, usually why value is null.

dimensions.description: Dimension code → {code, label}, one entry per dimensionsUsed code (e.g., {"geo": {"code": "DE", "label": "Germany"}}).

status.description: OBS_FLAG marker. Omitted when unflagged; confidentiality arrives in confStatus.

value.description: Numeric value, or null when unavailable, withheld (confStatus says so) or published as text (valueText).

valueText.description: A value published as text, verbatim (a PRODCOM unit such as "KG"), with value null; PRODCOM's ":C" becomes confStatus "C" instead. Omitted otherwise.

stagedRowCount.description: Rows staged; equals obsCount. Omitted with tableName.

tableName.description: Canvas table holding every matched observation, with flat dimension, label and obs_* columns. Call eurostat_dataframe_describe with canvasId for its columns first, then eurostat_dataframe_query. Omitted when nothing was staged.

timeRange.description: Period coverage of the whole match (what obsCount counts), so it can reach past the inline observations. An omitted bound is unknown, not empty.

end.description: Latest period matched, omitted the same way.

start.description: Earliest period matched; omitted when neither the match nor Eurostat reports one.

truncated.description: True only when the match exceeds 5,000 observations, the automatic staging threshold. Independent of preview_limit: observations can be a shorter prefix while this is false.

unmatchedValues.description: Filter values that matched nothing in the dataset, by dimension, as sent; the observations cover only the rest. Omitted when every value matched.

title: Query Eurostat Dataset
